name: CEILING.MATH
description: CEILING.MATH rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance, accepting any sign combination and adding a mode argument to control how negative numbers are rounded.
tldr: Rounds up to a multiple of significance, with a mode for negative numbers.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value you want to round.

parameters.name: significance
parameters.description: The multiple to round to. Defaults to 1 if omitted.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Controls rounding of negative numbers. 0 (default) rounds toward zero; any other value rounds away from zero (more negative).

basicExample.description: Round up to the next integer
basicExample.explanation: With default significance 1 and mode 0, 24.3 rounds up to 25.

advancedExamples.title: Negative numbers: toward zero vs away from zero
advancedExamples.description: Mode 0 rounds toward zero; a non-zero mode rounds away from zero.
advancedExamples.explanation: Mode 0 rounds -5.5 toward zero, giving -5. With mode 1 it would give -6.

advancedExamples.title: Round to a chosen decimal multiple
advancedExamples.explanation: 6.1 is the first multiple of 0.1 at or above 6.05.

howItWorks: CEILING.MATH rounds number up to the nearest multiple of significance (default 1). Unlike the classic CEILING, it permits any sign combination. The mode argument only affects negative numbers: mode 0 rounds toward zero, and any other value rounds away from zero.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: Only available in Excel 2013 and later (and Microsoft 365); older versions return #NAME?.
For positive numbers, mode has no effect; it always rounds up.
Workbooks saved for pre-2013 compatibility will not support this function.

commonErrors.cause: Used in an Excel version earlier than 2013.
commonErrors.fix: Use CEILING, or open the file in Excel 2013+ / Microsoft 365.
Use numeric values or numeric cell references.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports CEILING.MATH with the same arguments and behavior in current versions.

faq.question: What does the mode argument do?
faq.answer: Mode only matters for negative numbers: 0 (default) rounds toward zero, any other value rounds away from zero.

faq.question: Is CEILING.MATH available in older Excel?
faq.answer: No, it was introduced in Excel 2013. Use CEILING in older versions.

faq.question: How is it different from CEILING?
faq.answer: CEILING.MATH lifts the sign restriction and adds mode control; classic CEILING errors on mismatched signs.
